deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous passage of historical lecture or reading notes in German Kurrent, continuing from the previous page and onto the next. The subject is the history of the Seleucid empire under Antiochus III the Great.

The content, in order:
- After an eastern campaign Antiochus did not win back the lost provinces, but his position there improved.
- He fought Arsaces (of Parthia), dated here 213–210, and left him Parthia and Hyrcania.
- He marched to Bactria against King Euthydemus, who also kept his lands.
- In 205 he pushed as far as India and returned through Carmania.
- He then moved against Egypt (the Ptolemaic kingdom). Egypt, in distress, turned to Rome. Rome sent envoys to Antiochus, after which he withdrew.
- He then went into Asia Minor ('Vorderasien') and seized the Thracian Chersonese.
- Rome had just defeated Philip of Macedon and did not want Antiochus as a neighbour. It sent envoys telling him to withdraw.
- Antiochus answered that he did not need to (the sentence finishes on the next page with 'nicht', and the disputes continued for some years).

The only numbers are calendar years BC (213–210, 205). Nothing is computed. The notes resemble a student's transcript of a university lecture course on ancient history, of the kind given at Göttingen by Heeren or Spittler. Whether the hand is Gauss's own is not established from this page alone.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: Antiochus III's war against Arsaces II is usually dated c. 209 BC, within the 'anabasis' of 212–205. The notes' '213–210' is approximate.
Historical: Arsaces was not simply ceded Parthia and Hyrcania. He was confirmed in possession as a nominal vassal or ally, which is a simplification rather than an error.

Historical: in the Fifth Syrian War (202–195) Antiochus did not withdraw after a Roman embassy. He won at Panium (c. 200) and kept Coele-Syria. The statement 'worauf er sich auch zurück zog' is inaccurate or oversimplified.

Chronology implied by the notes is consistent with standard accounts: Philip V was defeated at Cynoscephalae in 197, the Thracian Chersonese and Lysimachia were taken in 196, and the Roman embassy came at the Lysimachia conference in 196.

transcription_corrections: 'Filipp von Macedonien' appears in the image as 'Philipp von Macedonien'.
Line 1 ('Er eroberte zwar nicht die verlohrenen Provinzen') and 'Er trat ihm Parthien u Hyrcanien ab' are confirmed by the image.
'Thrazischen Chersones' is plausible. The final word may be read 'Chersonesus', but the image is consistent with 'Chersones'.
The final line reads approximately 'Da aber Antiochus erklärte er brauche dieses', continuing with 'nicht' on the next page. The verb is uncertain and might be 'bedürfe'.
'Die schickten auch eine Gesandte' probably intends 'eine Gesandtschaft'. The image shows 'Ge-/sandte', so the abbreviation or slip is in the original.
